newsitem.title: CHINA: Portugal defence minister in China to boost ties.
newsitem.headline: Portugal defence minister in China to boost ties.

text.p: Portuguese Defence Minister Antonio Vitorino arrived in Beijing on Monday on a six-day visit aimed at improving ties and military cooperation with China.
Vitorino was expected to discuss the 1999 handover of Macau and NATO expansion plans in talks with his Chinese hosts but would sign no military agreements, said LUSA, the Portuguese news agency.
The Macau daily Macau Hoje said last week that Beijing was interested in selling military equipment to Lisbon, viewing Portugal as a gateway to the European market for Chinese weaponry.

Vitorino would visit units of China's three million-strong People's Liberation Army near Beijing, including an air force guided missile division, LUSA said. He was scheduled to meet Chinese Defence Minister Chi Haotian and President Jiang Zemin on Tuesday, and would travel to Xi'an and Shanghai later in the week, it said.
Vitorino's China visit is the first by a Portuguese defence minister since the two countries established diplomatic ties 18 years ago, LUSA said.
Portuguese-administered Macau will revert to Chinese rule on December 20, 1999.
